title: An Update on the Biochemical Staging of Nutritional Rickets: A Comprehensive Review
content: Nutritional rickets remains a significant global public health concern affecting infants and young children in regions with limited sunlight exposure or inadequate dietary vitamin D and calcium. This review revisits the biochemical staging system applicable to severe combined vitamin D and calcium deficiency. We propose that the classical three-stage model may be supplemented by recognition of a Nutritional Pseudohypoparathyroidism / PTH Resistance Variant—characterized by profound hypocalcemia, paradoxically normal or elevated serum phosphate, and markedly elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH)—reflecting acquired renal PTH resistance. Hypomagnesemia must be excluded before this designation is applied, as it constitutes a reversible and mechanistically distinct cause of functional PTH resistance. This phenotype is reversible with treatment and requires prospective validation. Evidence-based treatment strategies for each stage are summarized.
